items.sentence: The MHRA extended the UK authorisation of Casgevy to children aged five and over with severe sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.

items.sentence: The MHRA extended the UK authorisation of the gene-editing treatment Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) to children aged five and over.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: It is for severe sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: Casgevy was previously authorised in the UK for people aged 12 and over.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA says Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) can now be used in eligible children from the age of five with severe sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: Before this decision, the UK authorisation covered people aged 12 and over.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA describes both conditions as serious, lifelong conditions that can in some cases be fatal.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: It explains that Casgevy works by editing the faulty gene in a patient's bone marrow stem cells so that the body produces functioning haemoglobin.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA decision is separate from NHS access, which in England is decided through NICE.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.
